skill.name: installing-skill-tracker
skill.description: Installs project-local Claude Code hooks that record skill usage, prompt events, and verification results for later analysis.
skill.summary: Installs local Claude Code hooks for skill usage tracking and verification reporting.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most external-command findings are false positives from Markdown fences or hardcoded hook parsing with quoted data. Confirmed risks are persistent Claude Code hook installation and local logging of prompts, session identifiers, skill names, and verification status. No prompt injection text or network exfiltration was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Full prompt contents are written to local activity logs.
remediation.suggestion: Default to metadata-only logging or redact prompt text before writing prompts.jsonl.

remediation.issue: Setup installs persistent Claude Code hooks in project settings.
remediation.suggestion: Show the exact settings change, require explicit confirmation, and provide an uninstall script.

remediation.issue: Activity logs have no retention or cleanup controls.
remediation.suggestion: Document log locations, recommend retention limits, and add a cleanup command for old logs.

remediation.issue: Shell hooks depend on jq being installed and available in PATH.
remediation.suggestion: Check jq during setup before installing hooks and provide platform-specific install guidance.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Prompt Logging
semantic_findings.description: The installed prompt hook records full user prompts with session identifiers in local activity logs. This can expose secrets, personal data, or proprietary context if logs are shared.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The hook explicitly extracts prompt and session_id from Claude Code hook input and appends them to prompts.jsonl. The behavior is clear in the generated shell script.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Claude Code Hook Installation
semantic_findings.description: The setup script installs project-level hooks for prompt submission, pre-tool use, and post-tool use. These hooks keep observing prompt, Read, and Bash activity after setup.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: HOOKS_CONFIG defines UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, and PostToolUse commands, and setup_settings writes them into .claude/settings.json. This establishes persistent local monitoring.

content.value_statement: Teams need a simple way to measure whether Claude Code skills are used and verified. This skill installs local hooks and an analysis script for usage tracking.
actual_capabilities: Creates .claude/hooks and .claude/activity-logs directories in the current project.
Writes hook scripts for prompt events, skill starts, skill verification, and usage analysis.
Merges Claude Code hook commands into .claude/settings.json without replacing existing hook groups.
Records prompt submissions, session identifiers, skill names, and verification status in local logs.
Checks required files, executable permissions, jq availability, and hook settings with verify.py.
Generates a command-line usage report from local activity logs.
limitations: It stores prompt text locally, so teams must manage sensitive data and retention.
It requires jq for the generated shell hooks to parse Claude Code hook input.
It detects skill use through SKILL.md reads and verify.py commands, not every possible workflow.
It does not provide a remote dashboard, access control, or encrypted log storage.

use_cases.title: Track Skill Adoption
use_cases.description: Measure which Claude Code skills are opened, used, and verified during normal project work.

use_cases.title: Improve Procedural Skills
use_cases.description: Compare skill invocation counts with verification success and failure rates after users run workflows.

use_cases.title: Review Team Usage Patterns
use_cases.description: Summarize local skill activity before deciding which skills need updates, training, or removal.

prompt_templates.title: Install Tracking
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup in a new project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the installing-skill-tracker skill to set up skill tracking in this project. Run setup and tell me whether verification passes.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Existing Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether skill tracking is installed correctly. Run the verification script and summarize any missing component.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Usage
prompt_templates.scenario: Review activity after users work with skills
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the local skill tracking logs. Summarize invocations, verification outcomes, unused skills, and high failure rates.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Tracking Impact
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the installed skill tracking hooks. Explain what data is logged, where it is stored, and how to reduce privacy risk.

output_examples.input: Set up skill tracking for a new Claude Code project.
output_examples.output: Setup created the hooks directory, activity logs directory, tracking scripts, and hook settings. Verification passed, so tracking is ready.
The report shows that jq is missing and one hook script is not executable. Install jq, rerun setup, then verify again.

output_examples.input: Summarize skill usage after a work session.
output_examples.output: The analysis lists each detected skill, invocation count, verification success count, failure count, and procedural skill success rate.

best_practices: Run verification after setup and after manual changes to .claude/settings.json.
Review activity logs for sensitive prompt content before sharing a project directory.
Set a log retention policy and delete old activity logs regularly.
anti_patterns: Do not enable tracking in repositories with regulated prompt data without approval.
Do not share .claude/activity-logs with issue reports or public artifacts.
Do not treat usage counts as skill quality measurements without user review.

faq.question: What does this skill install?
faq.answer: It installs Claude Code hook scripts, an analysis script, log directories, and hook entries in project settings.

faq.question: Where is tracking data stored?
faq.answer: Tracking data is stored locally under .claude/activity-logs in the current project.

faq.question: Does it send data to a remote service?
faq.answer: No evidence of network transfer was found in the reviewed files. The scripts write local log files.

faq.question: Why does it require jq?
faq.answer: The generated shell hooks use jq to parse Claude Code hook input and write structured local logs.

faq.question: Can it track every skill usage?
faq.answer: No. It infers skill starts from SKILL.md reads and verification events from verify.py commands.

faq.question: What should teams review before using it?
faq.answer: Teams should review prompt logging, session identifiers, retention needs, and repository sharing practices.
